title: ばかり
summary: ばかり is a noun meaning "just that". Every use is a kind of exaggeration: just happened, nothing but, a great deal of, and the links ばかりか and ばかりに.

blocks.text: **ばかり** is in essence a **noun**, so it can take だ after it. Its core is "just this and nothing else", used the way English uses "nothing but": as a **hyperbole**. Seen that way, its uses stop looking like a list.
After a **past** verb it says that nothing has happened since: the action is very recent. The past tense is needed because the idea is about something completed.

blocks.jp: 昼ご飯を食べたばかりだ。
日本に来たばかりです。
blocks.en: I have just come to Japan.

blocks.text: 2. A great deal of one thing
After a noun it exaggerates: there is so much of it that it feels like nothing else exists.

blocks.jp: この町は観光客ばかりだ。
blocks.en: This town is nothing but tourists.

blocks.text: After a verb in the **て-form**, plus いる: you keep doing that and nothing else.

blocks.jp: 弟はゲームをしてばかりいる。
blocks.en: My little brother does nothing but play games.

blocks.text: **ばかりか** adds か, which here turns the limit around: "not just that, but also". **ばかりに** adds に and means **"just because"**, with a stronger and usually unlucky cause than から or ので.

blocks.jp: 彼女は歌ったばかりか、踊った。
blocks.en: She did not only sing, she danced too.

blocks.jp: 傘を忘れたばかりに、濡れてしまった。
blocks.en: Just because I forgot my umbrella, I got wet.

items: **Past verb + ばかり**: just did it.
**Noun + ばかり**: nothing but / loads of.
**Verb て-form + ばかり + いる**: keeps doing only that.
**ばかりか**: not only, but also; **ばかりに**: just because.

questions.prompt: 昼ご飯を食べたばかりだ。
options: I am about to eat lunch
questions.note: Past verb + ばかり: just done.

questions.prompt: 弟はゲームをしてばかりいる。
options: My brother does nothing but play games
My brother just played a game
My brother likes to watch games
questions.note: て-form + ばかり + いる: keeps doing only that.

questions.prompt: この町は観光客ばかりだ。
options: There are a great many tourists (an exaggeration)
questions.note: Noun + ばかり is hyperbole for "loads of".

questions.instruction: What does ばかりか mean in this sentence?
questions.prompt: 彼女は歌ったばかりか、踊った。
questions.note: ばかりか: not only that; more is added.

questions.instruction: What does ばかりに mean?
questions.prompt: 傘を忘れたばかりに、濡れてしまった。
questions.note: ばかりに gives a single, usually unlucky reason.

questions.prompt: 彼は泣い＿＿いる。 (He does nothing but cry.)
questions.note: て-form + ばかり + いる.

questions.prompt: To say "just did it" with ばかり, the verb goes in the plain past.
questions.note: 食べたばかり, 来たばかり.
Past verb + ばかり + だ.
て-form + ばかり + いる.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that means "not only"
questions.note: ばかりか links a second, added fact.
The recent action is in the past.
